newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Pound slips on UK budget, Dow damps shares.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Pound slips on UK budget, Dow damps shares.

text.p: The pound sterling drew no comfort from the British budget and slipped from its 32-month high against the mark on Tuesday while a tumbling Wall Street tipped European shares from record levels seen earlier in the day.

The pound, which has been riding high in recent weeks on hopes of further British rate hikes, slipped from a peak of 2.5586 marks to around 2,5500 after British Chancellor Kenneth Clarke told parliament he would follow a tighter fiscal policy to reduce the risk of higher rates.
Elsewhere on the currency markets the Swiss franc came under heavy pressure, pushed down by a combination of dollar strength and concerns about the banking sector.
It hit a 21-month low against the dollar at 1.2961 and a 20-month low against the mark at 84.84 centimes before recovering slightly.

Analysts said news that Union Bank of Switzerland, the nation's biggest bank, would take a one-time charge of three billion Swiss francs ($2.32 billion) to cover rising loan risks and would suffer a net loss for 1996, highlighted the chronically depressed condition of the Swiss economy.
Meanwhile the dollar eased from earlier highs in late trade, pressured by mark gains against the yen and by slipping U.S. asset markets.

Dollar/mark retreated over half a pfennig from an afternoon high of 1.53 marks after being boosted earlier by the weak Swiss franc and softer French franc. The latter hit as the French lorry drivers' strike intensified and as Bank of France Council Member Paul Marchelli was quoted as saying French interest rates should be cut as soon as possible.

On European bourses British stocks ended well below their early highs as Wall Street, which started off well, tumbled into losses. The Dow was 30 points or nearly half a percent down when London trading ended.

Earlier a sparkling overnight performance in New York and hopes for a fiscally prudent budget pushed the FTSE 100 to an intraday record of 4,094.4. But it closed just 13.8 points higher at 4,068.4 -- below its record close of 4,073.1 set on October 21.
In Frankfurt, German shares which ended bourse trade before Wall Street dropped, hit another record close, boosted partly by the firmer dollar, which makes German exports more attractive.
The 30-share DAX closed floor trade up 11.45 points at 2,810.64, off the day's high of 2,819.95 points.

But Paris French shares ended with modest losses, after a round of profit-taking accelerated by Wall Street's late tumble. Traders said the market had been looking to consolidate after recent strong rises but sentiment was hit by the worsening truckers protest and its broader effects on the country's economy.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.62 yen and 1.5245 marks against 112.62 yen and 1.5208 marks late on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 13.8 points higher at 4,068.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 2.06 at 2,275.08.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 11.45 at 2,810.64.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $373.75, well down from Monday's close of $375.05. Silver also slipped to close at $4.75.
